fun_highlights: The vocation system genuinely divides lives into distinct structural shapes. A soldier's life (Linnea Okonkwo: soldiering, war-grief, 3am flashback) reads like a different game from a scholar's (Cassian Ashby: hungry study years, the knowledge-hoarding vs. teaching fork, the scholar's peace at death). The five paths — blade/book/hands/road/adrift — produce lives that are visibly architecturally different, not just cosmetically.

Era-flavoured framing creates real world-texture variety without extra events. The 'y_calling' and 'c_origin' cards rewrite their prose wholesale based on the current era (war/plague/plenty/hard/turning). Dynasty 6's Ren Salvedi choosing the soldier's road reads 'There is a war on, and it is hungry for the young. Ren can choose a road now — or wait, and have one chosen' — a completely different emotional register from a peacetime generation's open-future framing.

Callback cards are the single strongest variety mechanism. 'cb_lookaway' returning in midlife ('Looked away a second time, and knew, now, exactly what it cost') creates a narrative arc unique to lives that passed the c_friend card a specific way. The 'child_books' callback at midlife closing the circle of the too-hard book is one of the most satisfying moments in the transcripts — Ren Salvedi reading it at 49, then Theda Quint at 55. When these fire, the life has a shape no other life has.

The epitaph system actively fights repetition with session-level memory and cluster-blocking. The RECENT_CLUSTERS and RECENT_LINES arrays across dynasties, plus per-dynasty look-back, mean the same epitaph text cannot land consecutively. Across 15 dynasties the epitaphs are notably varied: 'Left people gentler than she found them', 'Kept a whole country behind the eyes', 'Was, to the very last, difficult to discourage', 'Was poor in all but the giving of it' — genuine variety at the end of a life.

The collateral succession system breaks the love-marry-child template as the only way to continue a house. Dynasty 8's Noor Ashby explicitly chose no children at 28, then reversed it at 34 — two 'a_child' choices in one life. Dynasty 10's Anouk Ashby died at 9. Dynasties 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10 all run single-generation, creating a real rhythm of short and long houses rather than a factory of 5-generation dynasties.

The motto and heirloom accumulation gives a dynasty's session a genuine through-line that differs house to house. 'Nothing was given; all was built' (House Brandt, industrious) vs 'We burn bright, and we burn' (House Ashby 8, reckless) vs 'We do not save ourselves for later' (House Okonkwo, reckless-variant). Each dynasty's motto crystallizing around its actual play history is the most legible sign that the houses are genuinely different.
staleness: The 'Meet them halfway' / 'Pretend not to notice' love-opening choice appears in nearly every dynasty and the log-line variety is thin enough that the summary text reads identically. Across the 15 transcripts: Dynasty 1 (Iris), Dynasty 2 (Tobias, Edmund), Dynasty 6 (Anders, Linnea, Annika, Linnea Okonkwo, Naima, Calla Okonkwo), Dynasty 8 (Noor, Cyrus), Dynasty 9, Dynasty 11, Dynasty 12, Dynasty 14, Dynasty 15 — nearly every adult section opens with the same structural beat at the same life-stage. The framing card ('a_marry') has good era/vocation variation in its prompt but the love-opening card ('y_love1') produces functionally indistinct log-lines ('Fell in love', 'Found, without looking', 'Started, without quite deciding to') that do not feel earned by who the character is.

The body-decline observation lines cluster into a predictable late-life checklist. All long lives eventually hit the same sequence: vit_tire fires ('The stairs have started to ask a question of them' / 'Mornings take longer to arrive'), then vit_neg fires ('Each day now asks a little more'), then m_health fires (the doctor's letter), then e_last_walk, then death. In the transcripts this is extremely legible: Iris Brandt (age 81, 82), Cyrus Ashby (age 77, 79, 84, 86, 90), Niall Marchetti (age 71, 75, 78, 79, 82) — each elderly life cycles through the same physical-decline prose checkpoints. The pool within each observation is deep, but the structural order is invariant.

The 'a_bequest' / 'e_legacy' / death sequence forms a predictable late-life template that the vast majority of elder lives hit in order: legacy card -> bequest card -> garden/window -> last walk -> die. Dynasty 1 Calla, Dynasty 2 Greta and Pavel, Dynasty 6 Anders, Dynasty 8 Cassian, Dynasty 11 Yara all run this same elder arc shape with varying prose but the same event-structure skeleton. For a variety-seeker playing a long session, this skeletal template becomes visible by dynasty 3-4.

The 'cb_left_home' / 'cb_study_pays' / 'cb_lookaway' callbacks fire with detectable regularity. In the transcripts, nearly every scholar life hits 'cb_study_pays' with its two choices (Name your worth / Teach it cheap), and nearly every life that chose 'Go' on 'y_leave' hits the town-return callback. The callbacks are good variety mechanics individually, but because they are gated by common early choices (chose_study, left_home), they create predictable mid-life beats that a veteran player can anticipate — 'I chose scholar, so at ~35-40 I'll get the payoff card; I left home, so at ~50 I'll get the return card.'

The sibling card ('c_sibling') fires in a large fraction of all lives and the two choices ('Adore' / 'Resent') produce log lines that repeat visibly across dynasties. Iris Brandt, Edmund Ashby, Greta Ashby, Anders Sereno all get the 'Resent' log line ('Learned early that love is divided'); the 'Adore' variant ('Took to a new sibling like it was their own to raise') appears in Anders Salvedi, Cassian Ashby, Tobias Ashby. These two lines exhaust the variant pool quickly when reading 15 dynasties straight. The sibling card itself has no memorable vocation/era/trait variation in either prompt or log — it reads the same in war-era as in plenty-era.

The 'Move' childhood event ('c_move') fires too frequently across dynasties without sufficient log-line variation. In the transcripts: Henrik Brandt (age 5, 'Grieved the one you lost'), Ronja Brandt (age 7, same), Calla Brandt (age 5, 'Make the new place yours'), Idris Salvedi (age 5, 'Grieved'), Roman Lindholm (age 6, 'Grieved'), Ottilie Quint (age 9). Six of fifteen dynasties have a character who gets the moving-away event. The two choices ('Grieve' / 'Make new') each produce a single invariant log-line, so by dynasty 5 a player recognizes this card on sight and has heard both outcomes.

improvements.what: Add trait-aware love opening log-lines so the 'fell in love' beat is characterful rather than generic. A 'guarded' character's opening line should differ from a 'dreaming' character's — e.g., guarded: 'Let someone in for the first time in years, and was astonished by the weight of it' vs. dreaming: 'Had been half in love with the idea of them before the fact arrived.' The y_love1 text function already rotates 7 framings but the log-lines (in the 'meet them halfway' do) only use a single freshPick pool with no trait differentiation.
improvements.why: Love opening is the single most-repeated structural beat across all dynasties; trait-aware log-lines would make the same mechanical event read as a different emotional experience for each character, addressing the most visible staleness in a long session.

improvements.what: Break the body-decline observation sequence by making vit_tire and vit_neg trait/vocation conditional. A frail scholar who chose 'the book' should get different body observations than a soldier or a wanderer. The engine's observe() function fires the same pools regardless of vocation — but the frail/bookish/restless traits already affect stat drift (engine.js driftYear). Adding vocation-aware variants to the body observations (e.g., soldier: 'The hands that steadied a blade for thirty years have started, finally, to tremble'; scholar: 'The body sends its bill, and finds the mind a worse and worse negotiator') would break the universal template.
improvements.why: The body-decline checklist is the most structurally obvious template in elder lives, appearing in the same order in every long life. Vocation-aware language would make each elder arc feel like a continuation of who that specific person was rather than a universal 'human getting old' sequence.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 more callback arcs to convert the most common structural beats into payoff moments. The 'c_sibling' card fires in ~40% of lives but has no callback. A sibling-bond callback in adult/midlife ('Hendrik, your brother, needs you') or an estrangement callback ('The sibling you resented is ill') would give the card narrative weight proportionate to how often it fires. Similarly, 'c_sick' (the childhood fever) fires in many lives but has no adult callback — a midlife version that echoes the childhood intimacy of being cared-for could pay it off.
improvements.why: Callbacks are the strongest variety mechanism in the game (they produce unique life-shapes) but they only exist for a minority of common childhood/youth events. Extending the callback network to the frequently-firing c_sibling and c_sick would create more unique life-shapes without adding new mechanical complexity.

improvements.what: Add era-aware variation to 'c_sibling' and 'c_move' card log-lines. In a war era, being moved is 'The family packed everything because the front was coming, not because a better town was waiting'; in a plague era, moving acquires a different valence. The 'c_sibling' 'Adore' and 'Resent' log lines could get era/trait pools (warm/tender gets a fuller adoration line; guarded/restless gets a different resentment line). Currently both cards have single invariant log-lines for each choice.
improvements.why: These two cards fire in a majority of lives and their log-lines are the most verbatim-repeated text in the 15-dynasty transcript. Even a modest pool of 3-4 era/trait variants would reduce visible repetition significantly.

improvements.what: Introduce 1-2 vocation-specific elder events that have no equivalent outside that vocation. Currently the elder arc (e_legacy, e_garden, e_last_walk, e_bequest) is shared across all vocations — a soldier and a scholar face the same final events with only the e_legacy prompt varying. A soldier-specific elder event ('The old sword is still in the chest. A nephew asks to see it.') and a scholar-specific one ('A young student challenges the life's work in print; does the old argument hold?') would make elder-soldier and elder-scholar lives structurally diverge, not just prose-diverge.
improvements.why: Vocation variety is the engine's strongest structural tool but it currently operates mainly in youth-through-midlife (the calling card, the vocation-arc signature cards). The elder stage defaults to a universal template; extending vocation distinctness into old age would make the last third of long lives feel earned rather than templated.

verdict: A Life produces genuinely different dynasties and the vocation/era system creates real structural variety — a soldier's life and a scholar's life are architecturally distinct, and callback cards produce moments no other life has. The writing is consistently good and the dynasty layer (motto crystallization, heirloom accumulation, seat rise and fall) gives a long session genuine forward pull. The staleness problem is real but localized: the love-opening beat, the body-decline observation sequence, and the high-frequency childhood cards (sibling, move) form a recognizable template that a focused player will see repeat by dynasty 4-5 regardless of the era or vocation. The game is fun within a dynasty and fresh at the start of each new house; the ceiling on a very long session is that the skeleton of individual lives becomes predictable even when the prose rotates.
